title: Prefetch-Evict Coordinator with Transparent Audit Tracing for KV Cache Correctness
creator: Aisha Nadar
description:
Problem: As continuous batching scales and GPU memory budgets tighten, we observe intermittent correctness anomalies (stale KV prefixes, duplicated prefix reads across batches, and latency spikes due to uncoordinated evictions). Existing LRU/TTL and prefix-aware heuristics reduce memory pressure but lack a unified coordination layer and an auditable trace to prove correctness guarantees across concurrent request streams.

Goal: Implement a Prefetch-Evict Coordinator (PEC) that: (1) serializes prefix eviction decisions where necessary to preserve per-prefix linearizability, (2) provides a compact transparent audit trace for every eviction/prefetch action (for post-mortem verification and SLO-driven rollbacks), and (3) integrates with continuous batching to minimize end-to-end latency while bounding GPU memory usage.

Scope: Design + API for the PEC, runtime integration (GPU allocator hooks, KV meta store), audit trace format and retention policy, test harness for race and staleness scenarios, and a staged rollout with canary and rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: PEC integrates with existing KV store and can take coordinated eviction decisions without causing observable prefix staleness in standard regression suites
Audit traces emitted for every eviction/prefetch event and can be joined to request traces in tracing UI
End-to-end 95th latency regression <= 5% on stable traffic after enabling PEC for 30% of serving capacity
GPU memory tail usage (99th) reduced by at least 12% under mixed-length workloads when PEC is enabled with aggressive TTL mixing
No data races detected in the KV unit test harness that models concurrent prefetch+evict across batching workers
implementation_notes: Coordinator model: epoched lease tokens per prefix. Evict only when coordinator grants eviction token; prefetch obtains read lease.
Eviction heuristics: hybrid LRU score + TTL decay + prefix-affinity weight that prefers retaining hot prefix chains used by current batch windows
GPU allocator integration: async page release path to avoid blocking hot paths; reserver thread drains freed GPU slabs and emits audit events
Audit trace format: newline-delimited JSON with fields [timestamp, epoch, prefix_id, action, reason, requester, batch_id, kv_snapshot_hash]
Storage of traces: short-term hot store (72h) in internal logs for fast joins + cold archival to blob storage for 90d retention
Backwards compatibility: if PEC disabled, fall back to existing eviction path; make coordinator decisions idempotent based on epoch+nonce
testing_plan: Unit tests for coordinator state machine including forced lease revocation and grant races
Deterministic distributed tests using the race harness (simulate 50 concurrent batch workers, mixed sequence lengths) to assert prefix freshness invariants
Fuzz TTL and LRU weight combinations to verify there are no liveness regressions
Integration tests that verify audit traces can be joined to an end-to-end request trace in the tracing UI
Benchmark runs on a small GPU cluster (4x A100) comparing baseline vs PEC enabled for throughput/latency/GPU memory tail
Chaos run: simulate delayed lease heartbeats and verify safe fallback without corruption
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature gate behind runtime flag; internal alpha on dev clusters
Phase 1: Canary 5% traffic for non-critical models for 72h, monitor correctness and audit traces
Phase 2: Canary 30% with additional model families and run benchmark suite; if stable proceed
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 100% over 7 days with automatic rollback on invariant violation alerts
Rollback criteria: any observed prefix-staleness regression in production traces OR >2% increase in 95th latency for affected routes
design_decisions: Choose epoched lease tokens vs global lock: epoched leases are lower contention and map well to batching windows
Keep audit traces lightweight (ndjson) to avoid I/O amplification; compute kv_snapshot_hash in-memory via fast fingerprint
Hybrid eviction scoring chosen over pure LRU to account for TTL-driven expiry and prefix co-access patterns
Do not eagerly evict at request time; coalesced eviction cycle runs on separate threads to reduce P99 latency impact
tradeoffs: Pros: Stronger correctness guarantees and post-hoc verifiability; reduced memory tail under mixed workloads
Cons: Added coordination complexity and a small memory/CPU overhead for audit tracing and lease bookkeeping
Mitigations: Keep coordinator sharded by prefix hash to avoid single-point contention; make tracing adjustable by sampling rate
open_questions: What should the default audit sampling rate be for high-traffic customers? (ops suggested 0.5% as baseline)
Do we surface audit events in Console out-of-the-box or require an opt-in export to customer SIEMs?
How to integrate PEC metrics with current rollout hooks for automatic fallback when memory pressure spikes?
